title: IELTS Academic 21 - Listening Test 1 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

15:02ANNOUNCER: You will hear two marine biology students discussing a lecture on marine biodiversity and conservation from a visiting speaker.
15:13ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
15:49ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
15:58MAN: That lecture from the visiting speaker yesterday was good, wasn't it?
16:02WOMAN: Yeah, I learned a lot from her about ocean biodiversity. I've already done some reading on it and I did an assignment on some of the problems associated with it last year. But I especially like the way her lecture focused on more long-term issues.
16:20MAN: Yes, things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention but are likely to be important in the future. That impressed me too. It wasn't exactly a feel-good conclusion because it's hard to see any real solution for a lot of the problems.
16:36WOMAN: No, though she did point to where policy changes could be made to protect our marine and coastal environments.
16:44MAN: But that's just at a national level. The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are.
16:56WOMAN: Yes, me too.
16:58MAN: The research project she described was impressive, wasn't it? I'd have thought it was quite unusual to have so many experts working together.
17:07WOMAN: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds. Must have been a really exciting team to work with.
17:13MAN: I'd heard of a couple of them before. They were involved in research way back in 2009, warning about the dangers of ocean pollution. But now people are much more aware of that, aren't they?
17:26WOMAN: I suppose so.
17:27MAN: Another thing about the research is that the team members came from all around the world. Though I suppose that's not unusual nowadays. Now everyone can work remotely.
17:38WOMAN: Right.
17:39MAN: I like the way she didn't bombard us with figures. I mean, they were available, but she focused more on the general points they indicated.
17:48WOMAN: Hmm. And the description of improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals. And things like robots were really interesting.
17:58MAN: Yes.
17:59WOMAN: And her description of how robotics can be used to investigate threats to biodiversity.
18:05MAN: Absolutely.
18:09ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
18:49ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
18:57MAN: While you're here, can we talk about the list of resources we have to evaluate for the seminar tomorrow? I've had a look at them all, but it's been a bit of a rush.
19:07WOMAN: Yeah. What did you think of that article on invasive lionfish, the one claiming they were expanding their habitat throughout the Mediterranean Sea?
19:17MAN: Well, the writer went on about how dangerous they were in environmental terms, which is probably true, but he didn't really provide much information to explain why.
19:29WOMAN: I know what you mean.
19:31MAN: I watched the documentary on microplastics, at least I started to, but then I found it was made ten years ago, so I gave up.
19:40WOMAN: I watched to the end, but you're right, it was showing its age. People had hardly heard of microplastics then, whereas now, everyone knows about them and how dangerous they are.
19:51MAN: Yeah. Did you listen to the podcast on ocean pollution?
19:55WOMAN: Hmm, I didn't get anything out of it though. Most of it was stating the obvious. Yes, it mentioned pesticides and plastic and things, and it clearly made the point that they were a bad thing.
20:09MAN: But everybody knows that anyway. Did you read that book on coastal ecosystems, the one by John Harper?
20:16WOMAN: Yes, I found it hard going at first. It went into a lot of detail about things like the effects of offshore wind farms and fish farms, but actually, I ended up with a much better understanding of the issues.
20:30MAN: Yes, I agree, and I thought it was a well-written summary of those, and the diagrams helped a lot too.
20:38WOMAN: The article on metal toxicity was way above my head. I didn't know anything about how metals from industrial emissions react in the ocean, and I still don't understand it. I gave up reading after the first chapter. I just couldn't follow it.
20:55MAN: That podcast on floating marine cities was interesting, though it presented a rather one-sided picture, I thought.
21:03WOMAN: Yes, it focused on how this would benefit people and ignored the effects on the environment. But anyway...
21:16ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3.
21:19ANNOUNCER: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 25–30
groups.instructions:
What comment do the students make about each of the following resources?
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 25–30.

options.text: It provides a biased point of view.
It is too technical to understand.
It states information that is already well known.

q21.text: What impressed both students about the lecture on marine biodiversity?
options: A. It summarized problems they had previously researched.
B. It focused on issues likely to arise in the future.
C. It proposed viable solutions to existing threats.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (It focused on issues likely to arise in the future)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'focused on more long-term issues... things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention but are likely to be important in the future.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Nam sinh nói 'hard to see any real solution' (khó thấy giải pháp thực tế) nên loại C.

q22.text: What did the examples in the lecture help the students realize?
options: A. The national regulations needed to protect marine life.
B. The extensive scale of the threats facing oceans.
C. The localized damage caused to coastal environments.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (The extensive scale of the threats facing oceans)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are. WOMAN: Yes, me too.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'wide-ranging the threats' = extensive scale of threats.

q23.text: What surprised both students about the research project described by the speaker?
options: A. The wide range of disciplines represented in the team.
B. The remote locations where team members carried out their work.
C. The early date at which initial warnings had been issued.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (The wide range of disciplines represented in the team)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'quite unusual to have so many experts working together. WOMAN: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Về việc làm việc từ xa (remote locations), sinh viên nói 'not unusual nowadays' (ngày nay chuyện đó bình thường rồi) nên loại B.

q24.text: What did the students both find particularly interesting in the lecture?
options: A. The numerical data provided on endangered species.
B. The technological advances used to study marine life.
C. The methods proposed to restore damaged ecosystems.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (The technological advances used to study marine life)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals. And things like robots were really interesting... how robotics can be used to investigate threats...'
• Phân tích bẫy: Về số liệu (numerical data), sinh viên nói cô không dội số liệu ('didn't bombard us with figures') nên loại A.
• Đáp án đúng: D (It lacks sufficient explanation)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'the writer went on about how dangerous they were... but he didn't really provide much information to explain why.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'didn't provide much information to explain why' = lacks sufficient explanation.
• Đáp án đúng: B (It contains outdated information)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'made ten years ago... it was showing its age. People had hardly heard of microplastics then, whereas now, everyone knows...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'showing its age / made ten years ago' = outdated information.
• Đáp án đúng: F (It states information that is already well known)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'didn't get anything out of it... Most of it was stating the obvious... everybody knows that anyway.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'stating the obvious / everybody knows that' = already well known.
• Đáp án đúng: E (It greatly improved their understanding)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I ended up with a much better understanding of the issues. MAN: Yes, I agree...'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'much better understanding' = greatly improved their understanding.
• Đáp án đúng: C (It is too technical to understand)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'way above my head... and I still don't understand it. I gave up reading after the first chapter. I just couldn't follow it.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'way above my head / couldn't follow it' = too technical to understand.
• Đáp án đúng: A (It provides a biased point of view)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'presented a rather one-sided picture... focused on how this would benefit people and ignored the effects on the environment.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'one-sided picture / ignored the effects' = biased point of view.
